text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran the cont-batching + KV cache perf job after the slot-coalescer revert. seeing a reproducible p99 jump on long contexts (8k+ tokens). attaching perf notes below

troy: ugh. repro steps? can we get a flamegraph or perf record?

maria: repro command: `./testbench --workload longctx_mixer --batching continuous --kv-cache=on --slots=default --iters=200`
maria: perf record -F 99 -g -- ./target/release/infer --trace-kv=1

anika: grabbed a flamegraph. top of stack looks like batch-merge -> kv-copy -> page-fault handler. head-of-line blocking when batches merge different live spans.
anika: flame snippet:
```
  28.4%  infer  [kernel.kv_copy]
  17.1%  infer  [kernel.page_fault_handler]
  12.2%  infer  [batch.merge_batches]
```

leo: interesting — I also ran a micro-benchmark: when kernel selector switches to the int8 attention path + async KV eviction enabled, memcpy hotspots move to the host staging buffer. p50 stable, p99 doubles.
leo: bench output:
```
scenario: longctx-8k | cont-batch | int8-kernel
p50 120ms p90 210ms p99 610ms
scenario: longctx-8k | cont-batch | f16-kernel
p50 110ms p90 190ms p99 300ms
```

maria: so it's not purely KV algorithm — interaction with kernel selection + async eviction seems to surface extra page IO. looking at vmstat during runs shows high pgfaults/sec.

ops-bot: deploy 3976a1 -> canary-rt at 2026-03-12T09:12:05Z (slot-coalescer reverted) :white_check_mark:

anika: hypothesis: when batches merge, live KV slots from different sessions get co-located in a page, eviction watermark triggers, causing reactive reclamation during merge which stalls the head batch. that yields head-of-line blocking across merged requests.

maria: to repro deterministically i use two streamers that produce overlapping KV lifetimes and step up batch size gradually. after N=30 merges the p99 jumps.

troy: can you drop the exact trace id from perf so I can map to symbols?

maria: trace id: pf-20260312-11-3976543210. uploaded to /artifacts/perf/pf-20260312-11-3976543210.folded.svg

leo: quick mitigation idea: bias the batch-merge heuristic to avoid merging when eviction rate > threshold (e.g., >50 pgfaults/s) or when kernel-switch predicted to allocate host staging. cheap guard until we fix allocator.

anika: agreed. also experimenting with a KV-slot placement tweak: prefer packing same-session slots together to reduce cross-session page churn. local placement reduced pgfaults by ~40% in micro-run.

maria: can someone file an oncall ticket and add an opt-in flag for the heuristic? I'll add the reproducer and flamegraph to the ticket.

ci-bot: ticket created: INF-1427 "contbatch merge gating on kv-eviction-pressure" — link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-1427

ops-bot: cluster logs around pf-20260312-11: show repeated `kv_eviction: reclaiming 128 slots` entries right before the latency spike.

troy: ok i'll pick INF-1427. plan: (1) add merge gating knob, (2) add a metric for merge-block-duration, (3) run canary with gating enabled.

maria: thanks. adding notes: also evaluate kernel selection telemetry — if int8 path correlates with p99 regressions, we may need kernel fallback for cont-batch merges.

leo: one more datapoint: quantization tweak reduced host-copy by 30% in microbench, p99 improved but not fully resolved. points to a multi-factor root cause.

anika: wrapping up: pushing a small patch to pack session slots and adding a merge-gate based on eviction_rate. will post PR shortly.

maria: awesome. thx all — let's keep this thread for next-step perf numbers after PRs land. :raised_hands:
